THE PROBLEM IN ONE LINE

The Overview reports the day but never judges it. Eight equal-weight panels, every number absolute, nothing ranked — so "is today staffed?" takes a full scroll and some arithmetic.

The fix isn't more charts. It's a hierarchy: verdict → exceptions → context.

PROPOSED — same design system, same data, re-ranked

1. A status bar that states the verdict before any number.
2. KPI tiles that carry a sparkline + delta, so 89% can be read as good or bad.
3. Contract-mix donuts folded into the By-board table as one column, now carrying each side's share — 7 donuts become 1 column at 6 boards.
4. Two new modules: day / night split (per board, not just a chip) and host coverage risk.
5. The two near-identical trend charts merged into one with a metric switcher; the 600-character caption moves behind an ⓘ.

Missions with no crew are deliberately NOT flagged anywhere — that is normal here, not an exception.

BUILD ORDER

1. Day / night split — dayMissions / nightMissions are already computed in boardStats(); only the stats bar reads them today. Zero new queries.
2. Sparkline + delta on the utilization tile — the 14 days are already fetched for the chart below it.
3. Host coverage risk — one aggregate over deployment_history, the table added this week.
4. Position coverage — client-side arithmetic on employees.position.

Nothing here needs a schema change.

None of the four modules needs a schema change. Three are pure client-side arithmetic on data already in memory; host coverage risk reads the deployment_history table added this week — the same rows as the Host Record tab, aggregated by host instead of by employee.

Sample figures throughout are realistic placeholders, not live data: 128 staff, 21 missions, 2 boards.
